skills.name: Practical preparation: calculating time and date

note.text: A time-and-date exercise needs both an offset and a calendar check. Work in minutes after midnight to avoid mixing hours and minutes. Add the eastward time difference or subtract the westward difference. A result at or beyond the next midnight belongs to the following day; a negative result belongs to the preceding day. This guided practical uses ideal meridians, not current civil-zone regulations. State both the clock result and any date change when requested.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: A time-and-date exercise needs both an offset and a calendar check. Work in minutes after midnight to avoid mixing hours and minutes. Add the eastward time difference or subtract the westward difference. A result at or beyond the next midnight belongs to the following day; a negative result belongs to the preceding day. This guided practical uses ideal meridians, not current civil-zone regulations. State both the clock result and any date change when requested.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: A hypothetical point east of Greenwich is ahead. If the starting time is late at night, adding the offset may cross midnight. A point west can instead fall on the previous day when the starting time is early. In an exercise book, separate longitude difference, time offset, adjusted minutes and date change into labelled steps.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Do not discard a negative sign before deciding the date. Reduce the clock value to one day only after recording whether the calculation crossed midnight. A Date Line journey and an ordinary offset calculation need careful interpretation of the convention stated in the question.

key_words.meaning: the signed time difference applied to a starting time
the calendar result when a calculation passes the next midnight
the calendar result when a calculation goes before the starting midnight
expressing adjusted time within a single day's clock

examples: A learner adds an eastern meridian's difference to Greenwich time.
An evening time plus an eastern offset exceeds a full day's minutes.
An early time minus a western offset produces negative minutes.

mistake.wrong: An offset can be ignored whenever it is inconvenient.
mistake.right: time offset: the signed time difference applied to a starting time.
mistake.why: The offset is what connects the two times in the exercise.

questions.prompt: Greenwich local time is {clock(t)}. An ideal point lies {lon(to)}. Give the adjusted time in minutes after the starting midnight, before reducing it to a clock display.
Starting at {clock(t)} in Greenwich local time, calculate the day change at {lon(to)}: use {-1} for previous day, {0} for same day, {1} for next day.
solution: Compare with {0} and {1440}; the day-change code is {answer}.
